declarations.docstring: Right multiplication of the signed sum by a permutation in its supporting set scales it by that permutation's sign.
The square of the signed sum is its support cardinality times the signed sum.
There is a scalar-valued map for which sandwiching any group-algebra element between the signed and averaging sums is a scalar multiple of a fixed element.
There is a scalar-valued map for which the averaging-sum and signed-sum sandwich of every group-algebra element is a scalar multiple of their product.
There is a scalar-valued map making the displayed sandwich of every group-algebra element a scalar multiple of a fixed element.
Right multiplication of the averaging sum by a permutation in its supporting set leaves it unchanged.
The square of the averaging sum is its support cardinality times the averaging sum.
Left multiplication of the signed sum by a permutation in its supporting set scales it by that permutation's sign.
Left multiplication of the averaging sum by a permutation in its supporting set leaves it unchanged.
If a permutation is outside the product of the two displayed sets, then a swap in the left factor has the stated conjugation membership property.
The square of the right idempotent is itself.
The product of the two idempotents is the stated inverse-cardinality scalar multiple of a fixed element.
The square of the left idempotent is itself.
